story.name: Sales Elevator International - English
story.welcome:
Welcome on board {{company}}! As you know, {{company}} is a relatively small company with a vision to revolutionize the Elevator industry through state-of-the-art innovations. We have three products in our portfolio, the {{product_2}}, the {{product_3}} and the recently launched {{product}}. Your role will be to lead the sales team of {{product}}. Your predecessor was a complete misfit and left the team in shatters. He could not inspire the team to get their act right and our board trusts that your leadership experience will turn the team around. Information on the {{product}}, the parameters on which you will be assessed are attached.
Good Luck! 
{{ceo}}. 
CEO, {{company}}
story.overview:
{{product}} is the most recent addition to our product portfolio and we consider it to be one of our star products. {{product}} provides highest levels of reliability, convenience and its modular construction makes it very easy to maintain for our customers. We have been working on this product for the last two years and we believe this will be a step forward not only for the company but for the industry.
Initial feedback of the {{product}} has been encouraging and we believe that if you can motivate and inspire our sales team to perform at their best we can make {{product}} a star product for {{company}}. We are counting on the sales of {{product}} in order to achieve our end-of-year targets.
story.target: The target we've set for you are quite modest. You should not only meet but surpass them by a big margin! Good Luck!

briefing: As a people leader, one of your primary objectives is to help your team members perform at their best.

But how do you do this? Is there a recipe for ‘perfect’ leadership style one could adopt? Do you have to be hands on, hands off or follow any specific style with your team? The answer is ‘It depends!’.

Your approach on how to lead your team will depend on each team member’s skill and morale. In other words, great performance doesn’t happen when your team members need to adapt to your approach, but when you adapt to your team members’ needs.
There are essentially 4 different leadership styles:
DIRECTING- Give in-depth instructions to team member and hand-hold for execution.
GUIDING-Give guidance to team member as and when needed and seek buy-in to complete the task.
PARTNERING-Actively encourage and support team member in achieving task and take collaborative decisions.
ENTRUSTING - Delegate task by providing big picture and enable the team member to act independently.

Now that you know about the four different leadership styles, it is time to apply this learning in a virtual simulation - iLead. iLead is an award-winning, experiential simulation created by KNOLSKAPE, in which you will play a role of a Sales Lead handling a team of 10 members. Your objective in the simulation is to achieve target number of sales conversions and revenue within a specified duration.

To achieve this objective, you need to understand your team members needs and adapt your style accordingly. The simulation provides you various day-day actions that will help you interact with your team members as the time progresses. These actions when taken appropriately will improve your team members’ skill and morale, which further yields in good performance and results.

walkthrough.title: Tic Tock
walkthrough.text: This is your first day! You have limited time to turnaround the team and achieve the targets!

walkthrough.title: Meet Your Team
walkthrough.text: You will be working with different roles/phases across your team. Focus on all these phases to reach your goals. For more information about each phase, hover on (i) icon.

walkthrough.title: Know your team member
walkthrough.text: Click on each team member to uncover their background information. You need to know about atleast 3 team members before you can click on 'Proceed' button.

walkthrough.title: History
walkthrough.text: The results of all interactions with your team member will be logged in this column. Access this space any time you want.

walkthrough.title: Actions
walkthrough.text: You can use any of these actions to interact with your team member individually.

walkthrough.title: Leadership Style
walkthrough.text: Click here to set your leadership style with your team member. Make sure you do this for your entire team at the beginning of every week before clicking on 'Proceed' button.

walkthrough.title: Objectives & Tutorial
walkthrough.text: You can revisit Objectives and Tutorial anytime from here.

walkthrough.title: Leaderboard
walkthrough.text: Access this to see how well you are doing amongst your peers.

walkthrough.title: Notifications
walkthrough.text: Keep watching this space to view your team's responses to your actions, as well as future events. You can also view your past actions and responses from here by clicking on 'View History'.

walkthrough.title: Team Performance
walkthrough.text: Keep track of your team's collective performance here. Strive hard to improve these metrics.

walkthrough.title: Target
walkthrough.text: Leading your team successfuly will help you achieve your goal. Track how close you are to achieving your goal.

walkthrough.title: Analysis
walkthrough.text: Click here to analize your phase-wise performance. Follow the funnel and take wise decisions!

walkthrough.title: Actions
walkthrough.text: Interact with your team using the list of actions here. Choose wisely!

walkthrough.title: Action duration
walkthrough.text: Don't forget to make a note of the duration of the actions you are choosing.

stages.name: Sales lead
stages.description: Team members in this role are responsible for making initial contact with companies and collecting potential leads who may be interested in {{product}}.

stages.name: Qualify
stages.description: Once sales leads are collected, team members in this role apply certain parameters to the companies to check if they qualify to be potential customers.

stages.name: Proposal
stages.description: Once companies qualify, team members in this role send out proposals with pricing and service level agreements.

stages.name: Negotiate
stages.description: Negotiations with clients may happen with companies for price or for service agreements.

stages.name: Conversion
stages.description: Upon successful negotiation between client and {{company}}, team members responsible for conversion take over and process the order management system.

styleSheet.name: Directive
styleSheet.definition: You are direct with team member and give in-depth instructions.

styleSheet.name: Guiding
styleSheet.definition: Seek buy-in from team member to complete the task.

styleSheet.name: Partnering
styleSheet.definition: Encourage team member and help in achieving task.

styleSheet.name: Entrusting
styleSheet.definition: Delegate by providing big picture and monitor progress.

Once you get to know your team better, you may decide to reassign team members according to a task of their liking. Use this dialog to reassign members to different roles in the team.
Note: You may want to use the assess member action before swapping / re-assigning team members.
actions.condition: Each actor has associated skill, motivation and performance values for each phase. The new values are taken based on the new phase selected with a buffer of (+6, -6).

events.name: Tragic accident
events.text: Tragic accident strikes passengers in a {{product}} elevator in a high-rise in New York. This does damage to the brand, making it hard for the sales team to close sales.

events.name: Rumors of being acquired
events.text: There are some serious rumors that {{product}} might be acquired by {{competitor}}. The sales team finds it hard to convince customers that there is no risk of products getting abandoned even in case an acquisition might go through.

events.name: 360-degree feedback
events.text: In your 360-degree feedback, employees have mentioned that they're out of energy and are in dire need of a break.

events.name: Job offer
events.text: {{actor}} gets a job offer from your competitor, {{competitor}}. The fabulous pay package and promotion makes it hard for {{him}} to refuse the offer.

events.name: New microprocessor in the market
events.text: Engineering has introduced a microprocessor in the elevator that can beam the health of the elevator to service professionals. The sales team has not been educated enough on the new feature that has been introduced. They fumble when customers raise a question on the much-advertised feature.

events.name: New CRM system
events.text: Your firm has adopted a new CRM system and employees are forced to input leads electronically. Some are not tech savvy and do not like the change.

events.name: Tablet PC issue
events.text: Senior management has refused to provide the sales team with a tablet PC. Competitor's sales professionals dazzle prospective clients with slick presentation on their tablets. The sales team is also handicapped due to the lack of real-time information on the road.

events.name: Performance declines
events.text: {{actor}}'s performance suddenly declines. You find out that due to personal reasons, {{he}}'s not been performing well and could be a roadblock for others to act on their leads.

events.name: Business process change
events.text: A business process change in the company necessitates stringent sales compliance measures. This has introduced multiple approvals before sales can be closed. The sales team finds itself encumbered with needless paperwork, making them inefficient.

events.name: Recession strikes
events.text: Recession strikes. Salaries across the company are lowered and you (the {{learner_role}}) are asked to lower salaries of your team members.

events.name: Sales conference announcement
events.text: CEO announces that this year's sales conference will happen in a local resort, as opposed to the usual exotic destinations. Sales professionals expecting to cool their heels in Hawaii this year are terribly disappointed.

events.name: Strike at supplier's factories
events.text: The sales team is finding it hard to answer customers whose orders have been delayed due to a strike at one of {{product}}'s supplier's factories.

events.name: Insider trading scandal
events.text: {{product}}'s long-time board member, {{board_member}}, gets embroiled in an insider trading scandal. This brings a lot of disrepute to the company. {{actor}} tells you that {{he}} is embarrassed to meet clients who often ask {{him}} about the latest developments in the scandal.

events.name: Training Request
events.text: With new advances in technology, {{actor}} approaches you and has expressed interest in being trained in these skills so as to perform better in {{stage}}.

events.name: Elevator review website criticizes
events.text: An elevator review website criticizes the features of {{product}}. It claims that the features already exist in competitor's products and are not innovative.

triggers.name: Casual leave
triggers.text: {{actor}}: As informed earlier to the HR department, I will be on leave for the whole of this week.
triggers.rule: Check for an actor whose performance is greater than 70 and there's 1 more person in the same role. This event occurs only on periods 3,5,7 and sub period 1. The event should occur only once and the actor should be blur for 5 days

triggers.name: Clueless team member
triggers.text: You've reassigned {{actor}} to {{stage}} but {{he}}'s totally clueless on how to perform tasks in {{his}} current role.
triggers.rule: check if user has reassigned someone in the last week and the user has not sent the actor for training and the event has not occurred before.

triggers.name: Demoralized member
triggers.text: {{actor}}: I cannot work with my team mate anymore. I feel betrayed and coming to work everyday is demoralizing. Please reassign me to a different role or I would have no choice but to leave the company.
triggers.rule: Check for an actor whose performance is less than 20. Check at the beginning of every week after the 3rd week of the sim. This event should only occur once during the simulation

triggers.name: Lack of training
triggers.text: {{actor}}'s performance has been on the decline for the past 6 weeks. {{He}} blames lack of training in Sales as the primary reason. {{company}}'s HR Head is at the meeting and recommends that you should send {{him}} for a training and give {{him}} another chance, before firing {{him}}.
triggers.rule: Check for an actor whose performance is decreasing for the past 6 weeks due to various reasons

triggers.name: Medical leave
triggers.text: {{actor}}: I am writing to you to let you know that I am down with flu and would like to take a 2-day medical break.
triggers.rule: Check for an actor whose performance is greater than 70. This event occurs only on periods 3,6,9 and sub periods 2,3,4. The event should occur only once.

triggers.name: Morale drops
triggers.text: {{actor}}'s morale suddenly drops due to lack of recognition / awards. You find that {{his}} performance had been tremendous, but you realize that you hadn't congratulated {{him}} and {{he}} is feeling left out.
triggers.rule: If any actors performance is more than 60 consistently for 3 weeks and he didn't receive any congratulatory email

triggers.name: Resignation
triggers.text: {{actor}}: I have lost faith in your leadership and am tendering my resignation effective immediately. I wish you and the team the best of luck in achieving your targets.
triggers.rule: Check for an actor whose performance goes below 10. Check after 2nd week onwards everyday. This event should occur only twice during the simulation.

triggers.name: Role change request
triggers.text: {{actor}} has been in the same role of {{stage}} for the past 4 weeks and wants a change.
triggers.rule: Check for any one actor who's role has been the same in the past 4 weeks

triggers.name: Team member complains
triggers.text: Your leadership style with {{actor}} needs to change. {{He}} has not been performing well and has been complaining about you to others. You probably need to supervise, set role and goals better.
triggers.rule: Check for an actor whose performance has been decreasing in the past 3 weeks. This event can only happen on weeks 4 and 8

iLead, a compelling real-life like simulation, enables you to understand your approach to people leadership. In the simulation, you played the role of a Team Lead, working with a diverse team of 10 members, to meet the targets set for your team. Your objective was to enable your team to perform well by helping them build their skills, and to increase their motivation and engagement.

- This report tells you about how you performed in the simulation, on various parameters.
- There are several sections in which the information is represented in graphs and figures.
- To benefit from this report, relate the results to the simulation that you played.
- The Summary section provides you with questions that you should introspect and answer for youself.
- It also provides with some thoughts for you to keep as a guide when you manage your team.
This section describes various competencies that you demonstrated in the simulation.
This score represents your performance in each of the competency measured on a scale of 1-10.
Identify, hone and leverage team members' skills to accomplish goals.
Your lack of knowledge of your team members' abilities, hampered the effectiveness of your actions to hone their skills. You will need to put in more effort to identify your team members' abilities.

You were able to identify some abilities of your team members and hence few of the actions you took yielded limited favorable results. You will need to put in more effort to understand your team members' abilities.
While you were able to identify your team members' abilities, you will need to deepen it further to ensure that all the actions that you take to hone their skills yield the desired results.
You were familiar with your team members' abilities and you used the knowledge to effectively drive results. All the actions that you took to hone their skills yielded the desired results.

Your success is largely because of your deep knowledge of your team members' abilities and your timely usage of the right combination of their skills. This also ensured that all the actions you took resulted in an efficient and well-honed team.
Enthuse, energize and empower team members to maximise performance.
You were unable to understand your team members' needs. You will need to take more effort to pick actions that will maximize your team members' enthusiasm, energy and performance.

You understood your team members' needs reasonably well. The actions that you took to maximize their enthusiasm, energy and performance were effective most of the time.
You understood your team members' needs quite well. The actions that you took to maximize their enthusiasm and performance were effective.

Your were able to intuit your team members' needs and pick the most appropriate style to inspire them to perform. Your team members had become extremely enthusiastic and performed to the best of their ability.

You showed a good understanding of what your team members require to perform at a high level. Your efforts at creating an environment conducive to enhanced performance were effective.
You showed a deep understanding of what your team members require to perform at a high level. You succeeded in creating an environment of high performance.
Dynamically adapting leadership style to maximise morale, skill & performance.

You were not effective in motivating, improving skills or performance of your team members, by dynamically changing your leadership style. You will have to put in more effort to read your team members' needs and act accordingly.

You showed limited ability to read how your team members need to be managed at a given point in time and you were somewhat effective in improving morale, skills and performance by dynamically adapting your leadership style.

You showed adequate ability to read how your team members need to be managed at a given point in time and you were effective in improving morale, skills and performance by dynamically adapting your leadership style.

You were consistently accurate in reading how your team members need to be managed at a given point in time and you maximized morale, skills and performance by dynamically adapting your leadership style.
Ensure goal achievement through effective management of team members.
You were aware of the end goal. However, you could have taken more actions in leveraging your team members to achieve the goal.
You were aware of the end goal and you took some actions to leverage your team members to achieve it. However, you could have been more consistent in doing so.
You were focused on the end goal. While you took sufficient number of actions to keep your team enthused, not all of them worked.
Your unrelenting focus on the goal and your actions to leverage your team members proved extremely effective. Your team enthusiastically progressed towards goal achievement.

Your strong goal-orientation rubbed off on your team members. Your team was very happy with the way you set them up for success. Your response to the diverse situations and your timely guidance to your team members ensured that you surpassed your goal.

Morale and skill are the two factors that impact performance directly. Adapting the leadership styles, by accurately reading what team members need and the situation demands, can enhance performance. High performance drives results.

Good attempt! Though the target was not achieved on time, you tried to lead your team well. You would have been more successful if you had leveraged your team members' abilities, by adapting your leadership styles to your team memebers' needs and to the changing situations.

Well done! Though the target was not achieved on time, you led your team reasonably well. You leveraged your team members' abilities well and you were fairly adaptable in managing them in different situations.
Excellent! You have acheived your target on time. You owe your success to the way you leveraged your team members and adapted your leadership styles in changing situations.

The way a leader manages team members in different situations, impacts their skill and morale and eventually, the results. If the leader has consistently chosen the right style to managing a team member, it will result in increased skill and morale, and hence, better results. On the other hand, if the leader has consistently chosen inappropriate styles, it will result in decreased skill and morale, and hence, lower results.

-You demonstrated low levels of leadership adaptability. 
-You might want to invest some time and effort to get to know your team members well, so that you can adapt your leadership styles and manage them better across changing tasks or situations.

-You demonstrated moderate levels of leadership adaptability. 
-While you adapted your leadership styles to suit needs in some situations, you would need to choose the right styles more often in order to reach or exceed your goal.

-You demonstrated high levels of leadership adaptability.
-You adopted the correct leadership styles most often, and were able to change it as the situation demanded, based on the accurate reading of your team members' needs.

Here are some questions that will help you understand your actions better:

Did you give your attention to and engage with all your team members? If you did not, then why not? Why did some team members get more of your time and attention, while others got less or none at all?
Giving appropriate attention to and engaging regularly with all your team members is needed for you to drive results.
Are you unconsciously biased for or against some or any of them?
Biases, even if it is unconscious can be picked up by others and will adversely affect morale.
What actions did you prefer or were comfortable taking, and why?
The actions that are taken to manage teams may emerge from how you prefer to be managed.

What kind of actions had what kind of impacts on team members? Why do you think that the same actions had one kind of impact on a team member and an entirely different kind of impact on another team member?
Impact of an action is affected by the situation and mindframe of the team member. Continously communicating, assessing and adapting is critical to your success in driving results.
Thank you for playing the simulation! We hope you had a great experience. As we conclude, here is a brief summary of key points to keep in mind, and recommended next steps.
The strength of a good manager lies in leveraging his team members to drive results.
Morale and skill are both important for good performance. Performance drives results.
Keep communication channels open and get to know your team members better. This will help you take the right steps to increase morale and performance.
Constantly assess your team members and upskill as needed.
Give constructive feedback and coach as needed. Appropriate attention results in improved morale.
Challenge your team members. Motivate, support and celebrate success to enhance and sustain performance.
Take leadership styles based on your team members' skill and morale levels. Be adaptable to your team members.
